name: Codex
summary: OpenAI's coding agent for repository implementation, review, verification, and tool-assisted engineering work.
overview: Codex is OpenAI's coding agent for software engineering workflows that require repository understanding, code edits, command execution, review, and verification. On 2playclaw.com it should be treated as a serious implementation agent rather than a general chat assistant: the important question is how it works with local project context, skills, MCP tools, CLI sessions, pull requests, and team operating rules.

strengths.title: Repository-first implementation
strengths.body: Codex is strongest when the task depends on reading a real codebase, making scoped edits, running checks, and explaining the resulting diff.

strengths.title: Local evidence loop
strengths.body: The agent can keep work grounded in terminal output, file contents, tests, and build results instead of relying only on conversational memory.

strengths.title: Skills and project conventions
strengths.body: Repeatable workflows can be encoded through skills, AGENTS.md-style guidance, and repository-specific instructions so teams do not re-explain the same standards.

strengths.title: Reviewable engineering output
strengths.body: Codex fits workflows where changes must be inspected, tested, summarized, and handed back with clear assumptions and remaining risks.

extensionModel.label: CLI
extensionModel.body: Best treated as a terminal and local-project agent where command output, filesystem state, and edits are part of the normal loop.

extensionModel.label: Skills
extensionModel.body: Skills are the right layer for reusable agent behavior such as code review, debugging, documentation, browser checks, or repo-specific workflows.

extensionModel.label: MCP
extensionModel.body: MCP servers should be mapped as external capability providers for docs, data, browser automation, project systems, and internal APIs.

extensionModel.label: Workflow
extensionModel.body: Strong for repeatable engineering loops such as inspect-plan-edit-test-review, migration checklists, PR preparation, and release verification.

recommendedStacks.title: Implementation and verification loop
recommendedStacks.body: Use Codex with repo-review and browser/test tools when the output must be changed code plus evidence that it works.

recommendedStacks.title: Docs-aware coding
recommendedStacks.body: Pair Codex with current documentation tools when library behavior, API versions, or framework details are easy to get wrong.

recommendedStacks.title: Team standards workflow
recommendedStacks.body: Use skills and project instructions to enforce review style, testing expectations, and release discipline across repeated sessions.

limitations: Do not mirror generated install commands on public pages; link users to official setup and current docs.
Local coding agents can edit files and run commands, so permissions, secrets, and destructive actions need explicit guardrails.
A published compatibility claim should come from official docs, a source repository, or an approved candidate review, not from inference alone.
Codex is best represented as an engineering workflow surface, not as a generic chatbot replacement.
